labels.symptom: There's no way to hide apps you don't want to install or see in the launcher.
Users with a Taiwan or Hong Kong system locale get Simplified Chinese instead of Traditional Chinese.
labels.root_cause: There is no zh-Hant catalog, and zh-TW/zh-HK/zh-MO locales fall back to Simplified Chinese.

labels.symptom: When updating several apps, User Account Control prompts once per app instead of once overall.
labels.root_cause: Each app update runs its own elevated installer.

labels.symptom: On Linux, clicking Open in the launcher does not start the app; the AppImage only runs when started by hand.
On Linux ARM devices such as Raspberry Pi the app exits at startup with a WGPU limit error about max_inter_stage_shader_variables.
labels.root_cause: The wgpu device requests default limits higher than the GPU supports instead of using the adapter's limits.

labels.symptom: The app is not available on the Microsoft Store.
On Windows with Intel HD/UHD graphics the app exits silently at launch without showing a window.
labels.root_cause: Adapter ranking prefers Direct3D 12, whose shader translation fails on older Intel drivers, and the wgpu error is treated as fatal.

labels.symptom: The launcher cannot be installed through winget.
On Arch Linux, installing apps fails with exit code 1 because an .rpm package is chosen.
labels.root_cause: Package format detection falls back to .rpm on Arch.

labels.symptom: Legal disclaimer text does not wrap and is cut off at the default window size.
On Linux, the System appearance setting stays dark and does not follow the desktop's light or dark setting.
labels.root_cause: winit reports no window theme on Linux, so egui's ThemePreference::System falls back to dark; the freedesktop color-scheme portal is not read.

labels.symptom: On Windows, Start menu shortcuts often show no icon and cannot open the install folder.
labels.root_cause: The .lnk shortcut is created with a target path that does not resolve.

labels.symptom: Update all shows a separate UAC prompt for each app instead of one.
labels.root_cause: Each app update runs its own elevated installer one after another.

labels.symptom: Every app update on Windows asks for administrator rights, not just the first install.
labels.root_cause: Apps are installed in a location that needs admin rights, so each update needs UAC elevation.

labels.symptom: On Windows the app exits at startup with a 'device lost' GPU error unless OpenGL is forced.
labels.root_cause: The DX12 backend needs dxil.dll/dxcompiler.dll, which are not shipped with the installer, so shader compilation fails and the device is lost.

labels.symptom: There is no easy way to install the command-line tools from the launcher or Homebrew.
There is no way to sync or edit files through a self-hosted cloud such as Nextcloud.
There is no way to sync Google Fonts or other free font libraries.
On Linux the tray shows a random number instead of the app name.
labels.root_cause: The tray icon is created without a proper title or app id.

labels.symptom: User finds the interface ugly and asks for a better look.
The X (Twitter) button overlaps the GitHub button.
Japanese is not available as an interface language.
labels.root_cause: There is no ja-JP translation catalog.

labels.symptom: The web launcher only offers desktop downloads and can't install or run the apps' web versions.
Empty report with no description.
The app does not work on an older Intel Mac with Iris Pro graphics running macOS 12 Monterey.
There is no menu option to start an app headless with its MCP server, and no sign showing that it is running.
The apps cannot be installed into a shared Craft Suite folder.
On Windows, app shortcuts go straight into the root of the Start Menu instead of being grouped into category folders.
labels.root_cause: The launcher writes shortcuts to the Start Menu root and has no category folder structure.

labels.symptom: The macOS .dmg installer window has no custom background or layout styling.
labels.root_cause: The DMG packaging doesn't apply the styled background and layout used by the other apps.

labels.symptom: The interface defaults to 200% scale with no option to change it, which makes it unusable on 1080p monitors.
labels.root_cause: There is no user setting for UI scale (pixels per point).

labels.symptom: Request to add a new suite app similar to photomirage.io.
The launcher includes a web engine, which goes against the pure-Rust goal.
The macOS Dock icon is the wrong size or shape next to standard app icons.
labels.root_cause: The app icon isn't drawn on the standard macOS icon grid with padding.

labels.symptom: The launcher can only install apps with the MSI installer, not as portable zip versions.
Updating apps through the launcher unpins them from the Windows Start menu.
labels.root_cause: The update reinstalls the app or recreates its shortcut in a way that breaks the Start menu pin.

labels.symptom: On Macs patched with OpenCore Legacy Patcher the window flashes briefly and the app quits with a 'Parent device is lost' GPU error.
labels.root_cause: wgpu picks the Metal shader language version from the macOS version (metal3.2) rather than from what the GPU driver supports, so shader compilation fails on legacy drivers.

labels.symptom: On Ubuntu the app window does not close and the process has to be killed.
After installing from the Windows MSI, the app process starts and exits within about a second without showing a window.
After installing from the Windows MSI, the app never opens and its process sits using CPU.
On Linux, installed apps get no application menu shortcuts.
labels.root_cause: No .desktop entry is created when an app is installed.

labels.symptom: Request for new parametric CAD and simulation apps.
Request for a download-manager app in the suite.
On Arch-based Linux distributions the launcher tries to install apps with RPM instead of the native package manager.
labels.root_cause: Linux distribution or package manager detection falls back to RPM.

labels.symptom: There is no Lao interface language, and Lao vowel and tone marks may not display correctly without text shaping.
labels.root_cause: The egui text renderer has no complex script shaping for combining marks.

labels.symptom: The app cannot be installed with Homebrew.
One app installs successfully from the launcher but does not start.
On Windows, updating several apps shows one administrator prompt and one installer window per app.
labels.root_cause: Each per-machine MSI runs msiexec separately from the unelevated launcher, so every install asks for elevation.

labels.symptom: On Linux, resizing the window leaves ghost frames behind and sometimes crashes, leaving a background process that blocks relaunching.
Not available from Flathub, Fedora, Debian or Homebrew repositories.
On Windows the settings do not let you choose a custom install location.
AppImages always install to ~/Applications with no way to choose a folder.
Clicking GitHub links only opens the default browser without loading the repository page.
AppImage installations cannot be placed in a custom path.
The launcher names commercial products such as "Like Adobe Photoshop®" on app cards and in the table.
The launcher has no button to download an app's source code or copy its git URL.
The uninstall dialog stretches to the edges of the screen.
A tampered update feed could send app downloads to any GitHub repository.
labels.root_cause: Repo renames from the feed are followed without limiting which owner they point to, and assets are not bound to independently trusted checksums.

labels.symptom: Check for updates does not find an app release published a few minutes earlier.
Users cannot choose an install folder or drive for apps installed through the launcher.
On macOS a 'Where is use_default?' application chooser keeps popping up while the app checks for updates in the background.
labels.root_cause: notify-rust's macOS backend is called with the 'use_default' application identifier, so macOS tries to find an app with that name.

labels.symptom: A newly published app release does not appear as available in the launcher for some time after it goes live.
labels.root_cause: Possibly a stale ETag cache or a GitHub rate-limit fallback serving a cached release list.

labels.symptom: Installing several apps at once fails with 'error 100' for all but the first.
labels.root_cause: Each install ran its own pkexec package-manager call, so they fought over the package manager lock.

labels.symptom: No Linux riscv64 build is published.
On Windows PCs with old GPUs that lack D3D12 support, the app crashes at startup with a 'Failed to wait for GPU to come idle' error.
labels.root_cause: wgpu's default adapter choice ranks WARP last and picks the OpenGL adapter, whose old driver fails Surface::configure.
bug_markers: Failed to wait for GPU to come idle

labels.symptom: PR CI takes 30-50 minutes because slow FreeBSD and Windows ARM64 jobs run on almost every PR.
labels.root_cause: These workflows were triggered by lockfile changes and by pushes to main.

labels.symptom: Installing apps fails on immutable rpm-ostree systems such as Bazzite.
labels.root_cause: The launcher offered RPM installs through dnf, which rpm-ostree systems reject.

labels.symptom: App names and taglines are not vertically centred next to their icons.
labels.root_cause: ui.vertical fills the remaining space from the top, so the row cannot centre it.

labels.symptom: On Windows PCs with Intel HD/UHD integrated graphics, the app exits on startup without showing a window because of a shader translation error.
labels.root_cause: The adapter ranking prefers D3D12, where shader translation fails on Intel Gen9 integrated GPUs.

labels.symptom: There is no way to browse or install plug-ins from a store catalog.
On macOS a 'Where is use_default?' application chooser pops up when the app sends a notification.
labels.root_cause: notify-rust was never given an application bundle id, so mac-notification-sys looked up the placeholder app 'use_default'.

labels.symptom: On Linux the System appearance setting stays dark whatever the desktop's light/dark preference, and installed apps get no menu entries.
labels.root_cause: egui's ThemePreference::System depends on winit reporting the window theme, which winit doesn't do on X11 and many Wayland compositors.

labels.symptom: On macOS the Dock icon changes to an unstyled square bitmap once the app is running.
labels.root_cause: eframe calls setApplicationIconImage with the runtime PNG icon, which replaces the bundle's .icns in the Dock.

labels.symptom: CI workflows are duplicated in every repo and raise Node 20 deprecation warnings.
In narrow windows the header controls overlap the header text.
labels.root_cause: The header layout used window-width breakpoints instead of the actual remaining space.

labels.symptom: Connecting the apps' MCP servers to AI tools requires editing each tool's settings file by hand.
On Windows, an app installed by an older installer under a previous product name shows as not installed, so the launcher offers Install instead of Update and can't uninstall it.
labels.root_cause: Windows install detection matches only the current DisplayName and exe name, not the legacy PrintCraft name and paths.

labels.symptom: Installing or updating an app on macOS fails with 'couldn't open the disk image' and no reason.
labels.root_cause: A reused mount folder held by interrupted attaches, a slow hdiutil verify pass hitting the timeout, and tools run without full paths under a minimal PATH.

labels.symptom: The interface cannot be shown in Polish.
labels.root_cause: No Polish translation catalog or plural rule existed.

labels.symptom: On Windows, apps can only be installed through the MSI installer, not as portable copies.
On Linux the system tray shows a number instead of the app name.
labels.root_cause: The tray icon had no title, so the tray host fell back to tray-icon's unique id, which is built from the process id.

labels.symptom: You can't choose or keep a specific app or launcher version; it always updates to the latest release.
When the window is resized, the settings popup extends past the window and long buttons overlap.
labels.root_cause: The settings dialog had fixed layout without scrolling or wrapping.

labels.symptom: On Linux, updating an already-installed app from a Flatpak bundle fails with 'already installed' and shows a misleading Flathub error.
labels.root_cause: flatpak install --bundle was run without --reinstall, installs ran in parallel without a queue, and detection did not filter by host architecture.

labels.symptom: UI tests sometimes crash with a segfault when run in parallel.
labels.root_cause: A Vulkan loader race when GPU devices are created and destroyed on several threads at once.

labels.symptom: On Windows laptops with hybrid AMD graphics the app crashes silently at startup with an access violation.
labels.root_cause: wgpu's default backend order picks Vulkan first, and AMD's Vulkan driver (amdvlk64.dll) crashes when two driver packages register duplicate ICDs.

labels.symptom: After a .deb install the app still says 'Update available' even on the latest version.
labels.root_cause: The installed version was detected incorrectly for Debian package installs.

labels.symptom: The Windows MSI installer just flashes a progress bar and closes, with no wizard and no option to launch the app.
labels.root_cause: The MSI had no WixUI dialog sequence.

labels.symptom: The Windows installer does not let users choose the install folder or create a desktop shortcut.
The interface is shown only in English, whatever the system language.
No Simplified Chinese interface is available, and Chinese text has no font to display with.
labels.root_cause: No zh-CN translation catalog and no embedded CJK font.

labels.symptom: Launcher fetches release info from a central API with GitHub fallback and rate limiting.
On some Windows PCs update checks or downloads fail with 'invalid peer certificate: UnknownIssuer' and the app shows as offline.
labels.root_cause: The trust store was loaded once from the Windows root store with rustls-native-certs, but Windows only adds many roots on demand during chain verification.

labels.symptom: macOS installs and updates do not check who signed the app or whether it is the release's version.
labels.root_cause: The install path verified only the checksum and bundle ID, with no codesign team check or version comparison.

labels.symptom: A 'GitHub hourly limit reached' warning keeps showing even when nothing is being held back.
labels.root_cause: Any 403 or 429 response was treated as the hourly limit until x-ratelimit-reset, even when quota remained.

labels.symptom: On Windows, 'Show in Explorer' opens the Documents folder instead of the folder containing the file.
labels.root_cause: The '/select,<path>' argument was passed with Command::arg, which put quotes around the whole switch when the path had spaces, so Explorer didn't recognise it.

labels.symptom: In a narrow window, the footer's status text overlaps the links and icons.
labels.root_cause: The left side of the footer was laid out at full width before the right side was given any space.

labels.symptom: On Fedora, apps get installed as a .deb with apt-get instead of as an .rpm.
labels.root_cause: The package format was chosen by checking which tools were on PATH instead of reading /etc/os-release.

labels.symptom: AppImages stored outside ~/Applications or renamed show as not installed, and installed AppImages get no desktop menu entry.
labels.root_cause: Detection only looked in ~/Applications for the exact release file name, and installing an AppImage never wrote a .desktop file.

labels.symptom: Update checks and downloads ignore the operating system's proxy setting.
labels.root_cause: HTTP requests used only the proxy environment variables, never the OS proxy configuration.

labels.symptom: Starting a newer version just brings up the old version that is still running, so it shows an outdated update prompt.
labels.root_cause: The single-instance handoff didn't compare versions, so the old running instance kept control.

labels.symptom: There is no details page with screenshots and release notes for each app.
Apps can only be installed from GitHub, not from local builds.
On Windows, Update all asks for administrator permission once per app and opens an installer window for each one.
labels.root_cause: Each MSI runs through its own elevated msiexec /passive call.

labels.symptom: The interface is not available in German.
There is no Nix flake for developing or installing on NixOS.
Choosing Quit from the tray does nothing while the window is minimized; the app only closes once it is restored.
labels.root_cause: Tray Quit was handled in the per-frame UI tick, which a minimized window doesn't get on KDE/Wayland.

labels.symptom: On Wayland, the close button and Alt+F4 do nothing when the app is set to keep running in the tray.
labels.root_cause: winit 0.30 set_visible does nothing on Wayland, so hiding the window to the tray fails.

labels.symptom: Running apps whose path contains brackets or parentheses are not detected, so they can be updated or uninstalled while still open.
labels.root_cause: File paths were passed to pgrep as regular expressions without escaping.

labels.symptom: The launcher shows other companies' product names on app cards and in the table.
The interface is not available in French.
Inside the Flatpak sandbox, no app can be installed from the launcher.
labels.root_cause: apt, pkexec, flatpak and AppImage mounting are not available inside the sandbox.

labels.symptom: From the Flatpak or .deb launcher, Open does nothing, and choosing Flatpak still downloads the AppImage.
labels.root_cause: Commands ran inside the Flatpak sandbox instead of on the host, and the chosen package format was not respected.

labels.symptom: A failed install deletes the verified download, so retrying downloads the whole file again.
labels.root_cause: The downloaded file was deleted on any install-step failure.

labels.symptom: The interface is not available in Brazilian Portuguese.
There is no option to download and install updates automatically.
New launcher versions are not found right away at launch, and there is no prompt to update and relaunch.
After installing an app as a system package (.deb or .rpm), the button still says Install instead of Open.
labels.root_cause: RPM installs were filtered out, bundle-ID package names and multiarch suffixes were not matched, and the AppImage environment broke package-manager queries.
